prediction.likelyOutcome: The owners should recover substantially more than the State's $74,875-$96,206 position and likely land in the range Korman's cost-approach testimony supports, with some real risk the award is trimmed below his full $451,377 figure because the 65% depreciation was applied uniformly across acreage the State can credibly argue wasn't functionally affected by the taking. The exclusion of post-taking business-income evidence removes the State's best collateral attack and should hold on review.

Exclusion of Post-Taking Business Income Evidence

outcome.description: After a three-day jury trial in October 2018 the jury awarded $508,548 (exactly the owners' appraiser Korman's cost-approach figure and the low end of the owners' requested range), against the State's requested $74,875-$96,206 and the special commissioners' $74,429; judgment was rendered on the verdict. The Austin Court of Appeals affirmed on March 5, 2021, holding Korman's functional-obsolescence testimony admissible and the exclusion of post-taking revenue evidence not reversible. No attorney's fees in a Texas condemnation award.
